events.title: The draw for the qualifying stages of the 2006 Football World Cup is made. England , Wales and Northern Ireland are drawn together in group 6 of the Europe ( UEFA ) section, making the group three-quarters of a home nations championship - Scotland missed out by being drawn (amongst others) against Italy and Norway.
보카 주니어스 wins the Intercontinental Cup in FC 도쿄, Japan for the third time, by defeating Italy 's AC 밀란 on penalties (3–1), after a 1–1 draw at the end of extra-time.

리오 퍼디난드 received an eight-month ban from football and a £50,000 fine as penalty for missing a drugs test on 22 September. The ban commenced on 19 January, though Ferdinand was intent on appealing against it.

Irish charity fundraiser 존 오셰이 attacks 맨체스터 유나이티드 football manager Sir 알렉스 퍼거슨 as "greedy" for demanding £90,000 to attend a cancer charity function in Ireland in 1999. According to O'Shea, a sports celebrity demanding 'appearance money' from a charity is unheard of in his experience. Ferguson's appearance fee amounted to half the money raised. The fundraisers, until now unaware that Ferguson had taken half the proceeds, denounce his behaviour and say if they had known about it at the time they would have cancelled the event.

맨체스터 유나이티드 were leaders of the Premier League; their nearest contenders 아스널 (unbeaten) and 첼시 were four points behind. 찰턴 애슬레틱 and 풀럼 completed the top five, with 리버풀 and 뉴캐슬 유나이티드 close behind. 울버햄프턴 원더러스 and Leeds were bottom of the division; 에버턴 were comfortably clear of the bottom three. 노리치 시티 held a six-point lead over 웨스트브로미치 앨비언 at the top of Division One followed by 셰필드 유나이티드, 선덜랜드, 입스위치 타운 and 위건 애슬레틱.
